data.heading: Skeletal system
data.text: All the bones in a body form the skeletal system.
A young child has more than three hundred bones. An adult human has two hundred and six bones.
The skeleton also acts as a protective shield for the vital internal organs of the body.
The skull protects the brain from damage.
The ribcage protects the liver, lungs, and heart.
The skeleton works with the muscles and tendons of the body to help a person move around.
Bones are held in their respective places by short bands of tissues called ligaments.
A joint is the place where two bones meet or connect.
Two types of movable joints are called ball-and-socket joint and hinge joint.
The joints in the hips and shoulders are called ball-and-socket joints.
The joints in the elbows and knees are called hinge joints.
The joints in the skull are not movable.
